legend.label: Order
legend.html: Order · Order that will be queued or deferred

legend.label: Verdict
legend.html: Verdict · the answer of Limiter.Allow for this customer

nodes.label: Submit()
nodes.role: Entry point. Refuses, de-duplicates and asks the limiter about each order
outputs: Outcome: what was done with the order

transitions.when: stopped, malformed, a repeated ID or blocked

edgeCases.text: The ID is put into h.seen before the limiter and process run. An order that is then blocked or invalid stays in h.seen, so submitting it again reports Duplicate.
The two earliest refusals, for ModeStopped and for a missing id, customer or lines, return without calling tally. They are not counted per customer.

nodes.label: Limiter.Allow()
nodes.role: External rate limiter. Returns allow, defer or blocked per customer

nodes.label: process()
nodes.role: Runs validateLines, price and stamp in that order

rationale.text: `price` runs after `validateLines` because it multiplies each line's quantity by its unit price, and validation has already refused a quantity of zero and a negative price.

inputs: o.Lines: the lines of the order

transitions.when: a line has no SKU, no quantity or a negative price
transitions.to: the first drop bin, as ErrInvalid

edgeCases.text: stamp gives the order a sequence number before the order is routed. An order that is then shed, or refused by reserve, has used up its number, so the sequence has gaps.

nodes.label: Submit switch
nodes.role: Routes a processed order: defer, write now, shed or enqueue

rationale.text: A priority order whose write fails is taken out of `seen` again, so the client may submit the same order once more.

outputs: h.deferred, h.batch or a write to the Store

transitions.to: the second drop bin, counted only

edgeCases.text: The deferred verdict is tested before the order's kind. A priority order of a customer who is over the soft rate limit is deferred, not written at once.

nodes.label: h.deferred
nodes.role: Orders held by the soft rate limit until the next tick

rationale.text: A deferred order was counted in `pendingBytes` when it was held, so moving it into the batch reserves no bytes a second time.

nodes.label: flushLoop()
nodes.role: Every 2 seconds moves deferred orders to the batch and flushes

nodes.label: h.batch
nodes.role: Processed orders waiting for a flush; flushed at 64 orders

nodes.label: flushLocked()
nodes.role: Writes the batch to the Store; keeps it in memory if the write fails

rationale.text: After a failed write the batch stays in memory, so the next flush writes it again and no order is lost.

inputs: h.batch: the orders waiting to be written
outputs: h.pendingBytes: the batch's bytes are released

edgeCases.text: enqueue ignores the error of the flush it triggers. The order that filled the batch is reported as Queued even when the write failed.

nodes.label: Handler.mode
nodes.role: Load mode. Normal, then Shedding at the soft limit, then Stopped at the hard limit

nodes.label: pendingBytes
nodes.role: Estimated bytes of batch plus deferred, checked in reserve()
inputs: n: the bytes of the order

edgeCases.text: The hard limit is tested with the new order's bytes included, and the comparison is >=. The order that would bring the total to exactly 8 MiB is refused and stops the Handler.
A deferred order reserves its bytes too, so an order that is only held back can switch the Handler to ModeStopped.

nodes.label: Store
nodes.role: The Store interface that receives WriteBatch calls

bubble.html: Before any work, Submit refuses when stopped, malformed, a repeated ID, or VerdictBlocked. Each outcome is still counted per customer.
validateLines, then price, then stamp run in order. A bad line stops the order as ErrInvalid.
A deferred verdict holds the order; KindPriority writes it at once; in shedding, totals under lowValueCents are only counted. Else it is queued.
The batch flushes when it reaches maxBatch, on each 2 second tick of flushLoop, and once more in Close.
Once ModeShedding starts, nothing sets the mode back to ModeNormal. ModeStopped is just as permanent.
reserve switches to shedding at 4 MiB. At 8 MiB it stops intake and returns ErrOverloaded.
If WriteBatch fails, flushLocked keeps the batch and its bytes. The next flush writes it again.
